<reason>A provides the stronger case for limited streamlining: regulator-controlled eligibility, reliance on established evidence, and fuller assessment when concerns remain. It directly answers export pressure by acknowledging farmer exposure and restricting deployment where separation is unreliable. B raises useful challenges but never explains why rigorous screening permits shorter review within its own tiers yet cannot do so under A’s pathway. Its repeated equation of undetectable breeding history with impossible product traceability also remains inadequately defended.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s familiar-allele example defeats B’s “rigorous or fast” dilemma by distinguishing review of existing evidence from commissioning extensive new testing. B responds by attacking the separate regulatory category rather than identifying a necessary safety check that A’s pathway would omit.</best_rebuttal>
